# `mount_scan_port`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

List the cached serial ports available for the mount connection, with the current selection.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (strict; native handler, 64-bit build) |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0x83130 (64-bit build); selected-device stores near 0x25504, 0x25514, 0x25528 |

Copies the enabled entries of an existing cached serial-device tree into a request-local list and, through the settings getter, may auto-select an enabled cached entry (updating the shared selected device, name and ids and logging it). No device is opened or probed and no hardware command is issued. The reply carries each entry's port string and id plus selected_dev/selected_id, with the outer nesting unresolved. Params are not consumed.

Side effects: May write the shared selected serial device/name/ids and a log line; discovery/transport-description bookkeeping only. Cache population and freshness are unresolved.

| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply).
